newsitem.title: USA: USDA plans $23.5 million processed potato purchase.
newsitem.headline: USDA plans $23.5 million processed potato purchase.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said it planned to buy nearly $23.5 million worth of processed potato products for the child nutrition and other food assistance programs.

USDA said it expected to buy more than 51 million pounds of processed potato products, including 11.9 million pounds of frozen potato wedges, 9.4 million pounds of canned sliced potatoes and 4.0 million pounds of frozen oven fries.
USDA said offers to sell must be received by 1300 ET May 16 and the delivery dates are July 1 to Oct 31.

U.S. potato supplies in storage are 16 percent above last year and more than 17 percent higher than the five-year average, USDA said. It said returns to potato farmers are down eight percent from a year ago, while output costs have risen.
